area.hero.h1: Heating and cooling repair in Wicker Park, Chicago
area.hero.lede: Boilers and radiators, furnaces, central air and ductless systems, for Wicker Park Victorian houses, two- and three-flats, cottages and the lofts over Milwaukee Avenue. Family-owned since 1952, with the owner, Rob, still on the calls.

area.reviews.1.quote: Three times, my experience with Suburban Heating and Cooling has exceeded my expectations. The first time I found them as a quick search, my heat went out on a Saturday morning. He was here at 9am that day to fix it. Kind, prompt, and knowledgeable. He explained what he was doing, what he thought about my old furnace, and we agreed to keep fixing it.
area.reviews.2.quote: Great service all around! Carissa was polite and promptly scheduled my appointment. Rob came over and answered all of my questions thoroughly. The pricing was reasonable, so we decided to replace the AC and Furnace at the same time. We are so happy that we chose to do both at once! We were surprised that it was such a quick process to update everything.
area.reviews.3.quote: City & Suburban has serviced our HVAC system twice, over 5 years apart. Each experience was positive. They addressed our needs, answered our questions, and didn't try to upsell us. Both techs were very friendly and knowledgeable. Today, Eddie showed up when expected and fixed our AC within 45 minutes. If you call the office, you may not get an answer if they're busy.
area.reviews.4.quote: Rob and the team at City Suburban are top notch. I’ve been using them for several years now for annual checkups of my system and have nothing but good things to say. He is respectful of my space, my questions, and has always been punctual. No upsells, just what I need for reliable AC and heat throughout the year. They’ve always been accommodating meeting my scheduling needs, as well.
area.scope.heading: The same repair costs differently in a Victorian house, a two-flat and a loft
area.scope.1.why: Much of Wicker Park is a Chicago Landmark District, so a new condenser or vent in view of the street can need Landmarks review.
area.scope.2.why: The big houses on Hoyne and Pierce, and many two-flats, still heat with a boiler and radiators, a different job from a furnace.
area.scope.3.why: In two-flats split into condos, one boiler can serve every unit, so the owners agree the repair between them.
area.scope.4.why: Houses heated by radiators have no ducts for central air, so cooling usually means ductless mini-splits.
area.scope.5.why: Lofts over Milwaukee Avenue and Division run splits or rooftop units, so getting onto the roof sets the work.
area.scope.6.why: The biggest swing of all. Where the unit has years left, we say so.

area.buildings.heading: What heats and cools your Wicker Park building
area.buildings.1.title: Victorian house
area.buildings.1.body: Boilers and radiators, often with zones added over the decades. Central air needs a path for ducts.
area.buildings.2.title: Two- or three-flat
area.buildings.2.body: One boiler for the building, or a furnace per unit after a condo conversion. Condensers off the alley.
area.buildings.3.title: Workers' cottage
area.buildings.3.body: A small furnace in a low basement and tight duct runs. Ductless is often the neater way to cool.
area.buildings.4.title: Shop or restaurant
area.buildings.4.body: Rooftop units and make-up air over the Milwaukee and Division kitchens, scheduled around service.

area.faq.heading: Wicker Park HVAC, answered
area.faq.1.q: Does the old boiler in my Wicker Park house need replacing?
area.faq.1.a: Often it doesn't. We diagnose first, and where the boiler has years left, we say so. Replacement is quoted only when repairs stop making sense.
area.faq.2.q: How far is your shop from Wicker Park?
area.faq.3.q: Can you add air conditioning to a house heated by radiators?
area.faq.4.q: Does HVAC repair in Chicago need a permit?
area.cta.body: Have the make of your boiler, furnace or condenser to hand, and tell us what it's doing. In the landmark district, mention where the outdoor unit sits.

extras.districts.4.hvac: HVAC here: furnaces and central air in new builds, boilers in the two-flats.
extras.faq.2.a: Very close. The shop is at 1225 N Cleaver St, a fifth of a mile east of Ashland Avenue, just north of Division, and Rob runs the calls from there.
extras.faq.3.a: Usually, yes. A radiator-heated house has no ducts for central air, so cooling usually means ductless mini-splits. In the landmark district, plan where the outdoor unit goes first.
extras.faq.4.a: No. Chicago doesn't require a permit to repair, diagnose or maintain heating and cooling. Permits cover installs and construction, so a company's permit count says little about its repair work.
extras.faq.5.a: Monday to Friday, 6:00 AM to 6:00 PM, and Saturday, 6:00 AM to 3:30 PM. Call (773) 238-3838.
